context.description: An old slice that ended folds with its stop's state, and /task starts a new slice

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context Layer 3 review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM8a.spec.ts (committed b9553cc37d, unchanged); my own bare bun test run: 4 pass, 0 fail, 141 expect() calls. Given: the test stores two whole-spec slices in the old form; I confirmed against base 2c0214ab71 events.ts that the old FactSchema had exactly these 16 fact types and that run.started/run.resumed carried only an optional base. The test asserts the set equals the 16 old types, no fact has a path, the latest slice starts with run.started {base} and ends with run.ended {state: done}. When: each fact is applied through the real engine one at a time and through TaskEvents.fold; /task runs through the real TaskCommand.run with the real run job (only the session boundary and the job registry are scripted; the registry runs the real job effect). Then every stored fact decodes and folds: each fact decodes to itself via the current FactSchema and round-trips through the real event store (publish/read); each apply meets an active snapshot and returns a different snapshot, so no fact is dropped as unmatched, and the fold equals the harness fold. run.ended folds as a stop with its own state: before it the run is running with no stop; after it stopOf = {state: done}, run done, last history run running->done, unfinished units cancelled; the contrast run.ended failed gives failed with its reason. /task records run.started for a new slice because the old slice ended: sliceOf gives new, and the same facts without run.ended give resume (the causal contrast); the real /task appends run.started {path: spec, base: branch}, no run.resumed, the old facts unchanged, three slices with the new one latest. Every step is covered by specific assertions.
